lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Verify that the LinkedIn URL works and the contact details are the ones recruiters should use.
Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requires them.
items.because: They generally do not help a U.S. resume and take space from relevant qualifications.

items.says: Make the MBA graduation status clear rather than leaving it to be inferred from the dates.
Check that the B.A. entry’s date and location formatting matches the MBA entry.
Specify whether 35% is a relative increase or a percentage-point change.
Give the comparison period or test for the conversion result.
Check whether the result applied to all merchants.
items.because: Otherwise that scope overstates the evidence.

items.says: Clarify your ownership versus the team’s work.
Use “two weeks ahead” only if there was an established delivery plan.
Add an adoption or business outcome after launch if available.
items.because: It would make the bullet stronger.

items.says: Clarify what the $1.1 million represents.
Explain how the chargeback analysis informed the roadmap decision.
items.because: “Set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” is a strong causal claim that should reflect what decision-makers actually did.

items.says: Clarify whether you resolved the tickets or coordinated their resolution.
Give the queue’s starting and ending size if available.
An opt-in comparison cannot establish that the redesign caused an improvement without controlling for selection bias.
items.because: Merchants who opted in are likely different from those who stayed on the old flow.

items.says: Describe the measurement approach and its limitation accurately.
Explain whether all 2,300 merchants were exposed to the new flow.
Explain whether the 9-to-4-day result has a valid baseline or comparison group.
Keep the result’s scope consistent with the measurement bullet.
Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not itself reduce late deliveries.
items.because: It changes the calculation rather than showing an operational improvement.

items.says: Specify the measurement period or baseline if space permits.
Check that the 30% reduction can reasonably be linked to the changes described.
“Prepares” conflicts with the past-tense role.
Add the scale or consequence of the forecast work.
items.because: It currently reads more like a duty than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 hours is measured or estimated.
Identify the time period for the hours saved clearly.
Verify that “Present” is still accurate.
Clarify whether the project is an ongoing venture rather than an ongoing student activity if that distinction matters.
Distinguish students who had access to the app from those who used it.
Check that “first year” aligns with the project dates.
Clarify whether the 9-tonne figure is tracked rather than projected.
Qualify the attribution of weekly active user growth to pickup reminders unless it was tested.
items.because: The interviews establish the problem, but the growth does not necessarily show the reminders caused it.

items.says: Clarify whether 95% is an average over a defined period.
Clarify whether the reduction in staff cover shifts is attributable to the system.
Add what the working sessions delivered or decided.
items.because: Meeting cadence alone says little about your contribution.

items.says: Identify your role in mapping and changing the intake process rather than using passive voice.
Include a patient, staff, or processing-time outcome if available.
Remove the merchant first-payment bullet from the hospital project.
items.because: It duplicates the Harbor onboarding work and is unrelated to outpatient scheduling, making it look like an editing error.

items.says: Include “A/B testing” only if you have designed or analyzed appropriate tests.
items.because: The opt-in comparison may invite questions about whether you can substantiate that skill.

items.says: Keep the listed tools only if you used them hands-on.
Standardize tense across the resume.
Standardize date style across the resume.
Distinguish whether metrics are measured, estimated, or inferred.
items.because: That distinction matters more than making every bullet sound maximally impressive.
